question: Which connective tissue layer wraps around an entire skeletal muscle?
explanation: The epimysium is the outer layer of connective tissue that encloses the whole skeletal muscle. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of the perimysium inside a skeletal muscle?

options.A: Covering individual muscle cells to insulate them
options.B: Dividing the muscle into bundles called fascicles
options.C: Attaching the muscle belly directly to the bone
options.D: Storing calcium ions required for muscle relaxation

explanation: The perimysium groups individual muscle fibers into smaller bundles called fascicles. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the cell membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber called?
explanation: The sarcolemma is the specialized cell membrane that surrounds a skeletal muscle fiber. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why do skeletal muscle fibers have multiple nuclei inside a single cell?

options.A: They form during development by the fusion of many smaller embryonic cells.
options.B: They require extra nuclear control because they lack mitochondria.
options.C: They must constantly divide by mitosis to repair minor daily tears.
options.D: They absorb nuclei from nearby fat cells to increase their energy storage.

explanation: During early development, many smaller cells fuse together to form one long muscle fiber, which is why there are multiple nuclei in a single cell. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the main function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum in a muscle fiber?

options.B: Anchoring the ends of actin filaments to the Z-line
options.D: Transmitting electrical impulses to the cell surface

explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium and releases it when the muscle is ready to contract. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h3)

question: How do T-tubules help with muscle contraction?

options.A: They carry electrical surface signals deep into the interior of the cell.
options.B: They pump large amounts of sodium ions directly into the bloodstream.
options.C: They physically pull the actin and myosin filaments closer together.
options.D: They connect adjacent muscle fibers so they contract in sequence.

explanation: T-tubules help carry the electrical signal from the surface deep inside the thick muscle fiber so the whole cell contracts at once. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which structure marks the boundary of a single sarcomere?
explanation: A sarcomere is the section of a myofibril located between two successive Z-lines. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h4)

question: What happens to the I-band and A-band when a muscle contracts strongly?

options.A: The A-band shortens while the I-band remains completely unchanged.
options.B: The I-band shortens while the A-band stays the same length.
options.C: Both bands lengthen as the muscle fibers stretch to produce tension.
options.D: Both the I-band and the A-band shorten significantly in length.

explanation: During contraction, actin slides over myosin, which makes the I-band shorter while the A-band stays the same length. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which protein directly blocks the binding sites on actin when a muscle is relaxed?
explanation: Tropomyosin covers the active sites on actin so the muscle stays relaxed when not in use. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the specific role of troponin in muscle contraction?

options.A: It acts as an anchor protein that fastens the thick filaments directly to the M-line.
options.B: It binds calcium ions and changes shape to move tropomyosin away from actin binding sites.
options.C: It forms the core structural backbone of the thin actin filament helix.
options.D: It provides the enzymatic energy needed for the myosin head to swivel.

explanation: Troponin binds to calcium when it is released, which moves tropomyosin out of the way so contraction can happen. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h5)

question: What molecule must bind to the myosin head to make it detach from actin?
explanation: ATP provides the energy needed for the myosin head to release its grip on actin. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why do the protein filaments themselves not shorten during muscle contraction?

options.A: They slide past each other, which changes the overall length of the sarcomere instead.
options.B: They only shorten when the muscle is undergoing passive stretching.
options.C: They are rigid mineralized structures that cannot change their physical length.
options.D: They dissolve and reform continuously during every single contraction cycle.

explanation: Muscles shorten because the filaments slide past each other, bringing the ends closer together without changing the length of the individual protein strands. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T4#BMP111_U3_T4_h6)
